# EV Charging Stations (OCPP 1.6/2.0.1, OCPI Roaming) & Battery Swapping Cabinets (`ev-charging-ocpp-ocpi-battery`)

> **Group:** IV. IoT, Automotive, Robotics & OT
> **Product Archetypes:** EV_Charging_CSMS_OCPP, IoT_Telematics_Broker
> **Trigger Signals:** ocpp, ocpi, charging, charger, evse, csms, cpola, vgreen, battery, swap, kwh, metervalues

## [ BLOCK: ocpp-security-profiles-and-billing-integrity ]
### OCPP WebSocket Authentication, MeterValues Billing Integrity & Franchise Revenue
- Check whether OCPP endpoints use plain `ws://` or enforce `wss://` with client certificates (OCPP Security Profile 2/3).
- Trace `StartTransaction`, `StopTransaction`, and `MeterValues`: verify whether a spoofed charger or MITM can inflate kWh readings to defraud free-charging subsidies or franchise revenue sharing (e.g., 750 VND/kWh).

## [ BLOCK: remote-battery-lock-and-cabinet-actuation ]
### Remote Battery Kill-Switch, Cabinet Unlock & Roaming Bus (OCPI)
- Audit authentication, multi-party authorization, and immutable audit logging on remote battery locking/disabling commands and cabinet door/charging actuation.

## [ BLOCK: ocpp-session-token-revocation-and-rate-limiting ]
### Charger Identity Revocation, Message Rate-Limiting & Audit Tampering
- Verify that decommissioned or compromised chargeBoxIds have their TLS client certificates / Basic Auth credentials immediately revoked (ASVS V7).
- Check OCPP WebSocket handlers for message flood / payload size rate-limiting (API4) and tamper-evident logging of all `RemoteStartTransaction`, `RemoteStopTransaction`, `ChangeConfiguration`, and `UpdateFirmware` commands (ASVS V16).

### Standard Mappings
- OCPP-2.0.1-SecurityProfile3, ISO-15118, IEC-62443-4-2, OWASP-API1:2023, OWASP-API4:2023, ASVS-V7, ASVS-V16

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- OCPP over wss:// with Security Profile 2/3 client certificate binding chargeBoxId to the authenticated TLS certificate CN
- Signed meter values (OCMF) and monotonic kWh delta validation before calculating billing or franchise subsidies
- Signed firmware URLs and multi-party authorization with immutable audit logs for battery lock/unlock and cabinet actuation

### Vulnerable Patterns
- Plain ws:// OCPP connections or accepting any chargeBoxId in the WebSocket URL path without matching credentials/certificate
- Trusting unverified MeterValues payloads from chargers to compute high-value franchise payouts or free-charging credits
- Unauthenticated or BOLA-vulnerable HTTP endpoints triggering RemoteStartTransaction, RemoteStopTransaction, or battery cabinet unlock

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of OCPP WebSocket upgrade/authentication handler and message dispatcher
- ev_... excerpt of billing/MeterValues calculation or remote charging/battery actuation API handler

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Does an upstream mTLS termination proxy validate charger client certificates and inject the verified CN header before reaching the CSMS?
- Does the physical battery swapping cabinet BMS enforce local thermal and current-limit interlocks during charging/unlocking?
